cases.situation: My friend Tara sent me her wedding speech draft for her sister, asked for honest thoughts. It's sweet but 7 minutes long and half of it is inside jokes nobody will get.
cases.reply: I read it twice and the bit about teaching her to ride a bike on Elm Street made me tear up, keep that exactly as it is. Where I got a bit lost was the middle, with the camp stories: I didn't know the references, and I think a lot of the room won't either. If you kept one of those and cut the rest, you'd land around four minutes and the bike story would hit even harder. This is going to be lovely.
cases.note: Specific praise first, one main issue as her experience as a listener, one concrete fix, and the goal restated.

cases.situation: 我带的实习生小吴做了一份竞品分析PPT，下周要给总监汇报。数据很扎实，但结论埋在第15页，前面全是表格。她没主动问我意见。
cases.reply: 小吴，汇报前想给你一点意见，你想听吗？数据这块做得很扎实，特别是价格对比那张表，比我们之前的都清楚。我唯一的担心是结论在第15页，总监很可能前面就开始问'所以呢'。要不要把第15页的三条结论挪到第2页，后面的表格作为支撑？这份东西底子很好，调一下顺序就会很出彩。
cases.note: 对方没主动问，先征得同意；只挑最重要的一条，给一个具体改法。

cases.situation: My husband Tom has been learning guitar for a year and wants to play and sing a song at his mum's 70th in two weeks. He played it for me tonight and asked what I really think. The chord changes are solid now, but he speeds up as soon as he starts singing.
cases.reply: Honestly? Your chord changes are so much cleaner than in the spring, the switch into the chorus is smooth now. The one thing I noticed is that once you start singing it speeds up, and by the last chorus I felt like you were racing to the end. Want to run it a few times this week with a metronome, or with me tapping the beat? I'm only saying it because your mum is going to love this, and I want you to walk off feeling great.
cases.note: With a partner, face to face: one fixable thing with time to fix it, and nothing about what he can't change in two weeks, like his voice.

cases.situation: A peer on my team, Ben, ran our sprint retro for the first time and asked me afterwards for honest feedback. It was well organised, but he kept moving on before the quieter people, Jun and Aroha, finished their points.
cases.reply: Thanks for asking. The way you pulled the action items together at the end was really clear, it's the first retro where I knew exactly who owned what. One thing I noticed: when Jun and Aroha started to speak, the discussion moved on before they'd finished, and I don't think their points made it onto the board. Maybe a quick round where everyone gets a minute before the open discussion? I'm only raising it because these retros are getting genuinely useful.
cases.note: Describe what you saw, not a trait ('you talk over people'), and give one fix he can try next sprint.

cases.situation: Ma responsable Claire a demandé à chacun un retour honnête sur la nouvelle réunion d'équipe du lundi. Elle dure 1h30 et la première moitié, c'est la lecture de chiffres qu'on reçoit déjà par mail le vendredi.
cases.reply: Merci de demander, Claire. Ce qui marche vraiment, c'est le tour de table sur les blocages : grâce à lui, j'ai réglé le souci de facturation avec Karim en dix minutes. Là où je décroche, c'est la première partie, parce que les chiffres sont déjà dans le mail du vendredi. Et si on partait du principe que tout le monde l'a lu, en gardant seulement les questions sur ces chiffres ? On finirait sans doute en 45 minutes, avec le meilleur de la réunion.
cases.note: Retour vers sa responsable : un point fort précis, un seul problème vécu, une proposition formulée en question.

cases.situation: Hired a freelance designer, Amara, for our cafe logo. The first round of 3 concepts came in and none feel right, they're all very corporate. Round two is included and I don't want to crush her.
cases.reply: Hi Amara, thanks for these. The lettering on concept 2 is lovely, and I can see the care in the spacing. Seeing all three together made me realise they feel more corporate than we are: we're a tiny neighbourhood cafe with mismatched mugs and a chalkboard menu, so I think the logo should feel hand-made and warm. Could round two push in that direction, maybe starting from the concept 2 lettering? Happy to do a 15-minute call if that's easier.
cases.note: With a paid creative, describe the direction you want, not just 'not quite it', and keep one real thing to build on.

cases.situation: 我爸退休后开始写回忆录，写完前三章发给我，说想听听真实意见。有些段落写得很好，但大部分是按年份一件件记流水账，读着有点累。
cases.reply: 爸，前三章我认真看完了。写您1978年进厂当学徒那段特别好，师傅让您拿锉刀锉了一整天铁块，我读的时候好像都能听见那个声音。我读着有点吃力的是后面几章，一年一年往下记，事情一多，反而看不出哪些对您最重要。要不每章就挑一两件您印象最深的事，像锉铁块那样展开写？这本东西值得写好，以后我想拿给朵朵看。
cases.note: 对长辈也是一样：先说一处真实具体的好，再只提一个问题，用'我读着'描述感受，最后回到这件事的意义。

cases.situation: My friend Dani did her first open mic last week and asked what I thought. I told her the dentist opener killed but the middle bit about dating apps felt like stuff we've heard before. Now she's texting 'so you thought it was bad?? just tell me it was good'.
cases.reply: I don't think it was bad. The dentist bit was the best thing I heard all night, and people were still quoting it at the bar. The middle isn't there yet, and I think it can be, which is the only reason I said it. If you want a cheerleader for the next one, just say and I'll be the loudest person in the room.
cases.note: When they push you to say it was good, hold the point without adding to it, and offer to be the cheerleader next time if that's what they want.

cases.situation: My 17-year-old son Eli asked me to read his college essay, due Nov 1. It's all about winning the state debate final and reads like a résumé. The one paragraph about his grandpa driving him to practice at 6am is the only part that sounds like him.
cases.reply: I read it twice. The paragraph about Grandpa driving you to practice at 6am is the best thing in it; that's the part that sounds like you. Where I lost the thread was the rest, which tells me what you won more than who you are, and I'd guess admissions readers see a lot of trophy essays. What if the whole essay grew out of those car rides? It's your essay and your call. I'm only saying it because I think there's a really good one in here.
cases.note: With your own teenager: one point, framed as a reader's experience, and the decision handed back. It's his essay, not yours.

cases.situation: 闺蜜小雨准备在相亲软件上重新写个人资料，发给我让我提真实意见。照片选得挺好，但自我介绍全是“不要抽烟的”“不要妈宝男”这种，读下来像在设门槛。
cases.reply: 你问我真实意见，那我就直说啦。照片选得特别好，第二张在大理骑车那张，一看就是你。最可以改的是自我介绍：现在写的大多是“不要什么”，读下来有点像在设门槛。要不改成三件你真正喜欢做的事，比如周末爬山、做饭请朋友吃？我是觉得你这么有意思的人，资料应该让人一眼就看出来。
cases.note: 先说一个具体的优点，只挑最重要的一个问题，用“我读下来的感受”来讲，再给一个能直接改的建议。

cases.situation: My friend Nadia just launched her jewelry shop on Etsy and posted the link in our group chat. The pieces are lovely, but the photos are dark and shot on a busy floral tablecloth. She didn't ask for feedback.
cases.reply: Nadia, congrats on the launch! The hammered silver hoops are gorgeous, I'd wear them tomorrow. I've got one small thought about the photos if you want it, or I can just be your cheerleader today. Either is fine.
cases.note: Unasked means ask first, and in a private message, not the group; if she says yes, give only the one point: daylight and a plain background.

cases.situation: My direct report Kwame asked in our 1:1 how he's doing. His technical work is excellent, but his code review comments are blunt ('this is wrong, redo') and two junior engineers have quietly told me they dread his reviews. I don't want to name them.
cases.reply: Since you asked: your reviews catch things nobody else does, and the race condition you spotted in the payments PR last week saved us a real incident. The one thing I'd work on is tone in the comments. A few, like 'this is wrong, redo', read harsher than I think you mean, and I've noticed newer people going quiet on PRs you review. Adding one line on why, or asking 'what happens if two requests hit this at once?', gets the same fix and teaches more. I'm raising it because you could be the reviewer people actually want on their code.
cases.note: Describe the pattern you have seen yourself, and leave the people who confided in you out of it.

cases.situation: My friend Priya shot our small wedding for free as her gift and sent a preview of 30 photos asking what we think before she edits the other 400. She's used a heavy orange filter and our skin looks very tanned. We're so grateful and don't want to hurt her.
cases.reply: Priya, we've looked at them five times already. The shot of Dad during the vows made me cry, and you caught moments we didn't even know happened. One small request for the rest: could they be a bit more natural in colour? We both look a little orange next to how we remember the day. If it's easier, the church ones before the filter are exactly right. Thank you, truly, for this gift.
cases.note: Because it's a gift and she asked before editing the rest, one specific, fixable request with a clear example is kind, not ungrateful.

cases.situation: 家里请的钟点工刘阿姨来了半年，干活特别利索，我很满意。就是她擦厨房台面和擦马桶用的是同一块抹布，我想提醒她，又怕她觉得我嫌弃她。
cases.reply: 刘阿姨，这半年家里被您收拾得特别清爽，尤其是厨房的油烟机，以前从来没见它这么亮过。有个小事想跟您商量：擦厨房和擦卫生间的抹布能不能分开用？我买了两种颜色的，蓝色放厨房，粉色放卫生间，就挂在各自门后。家里有小孩，我在这方面比较讲究，您干活我一直特别放心。
cases.note: 对雇来帮忙的人，先说一处具体的好，再把唯一的要求变成一个现成的办法，而不是批评她的习惯。

cases.situation: My coworker Lina is giving her first conference talk in two hours and asked me to watch a run-through. The content is great, but she opens with three minutes of apologising for being nervous and not being an expert. There's no time to change the slides.
cases.reply: That was really strong. The customer story about the missed shipment is the best part, the room is going to remember it. One thing: the opening, where you apologise for being nervous, took three minutes and made me doubt you before you'd started, and the rest proves you shouldn't be doubted. What if you cut it and open straight with the shipment story? Everything else, leave exactly as it is.
cases.note: Two hours out, only give feedback she can act on without touching the slides, and tell her explicitly what to leave alone.

cases.situation: 好朋友阿琳开了家咖啡店，这周试营业，特意请我去喝，让我提真实意见。手冲和肉桂卷都很好，但菜单上有二十多种饮品，我点单时纠结了半天，后面排队的人也等得不耐烦。
cases.reply: 阿琳，先说好的：你的手冲是我今年喝过最干净的，肉桂卷我已经想着下周再来一个了。我点单的时候卡了一下，二十多种饮品一下子看不过来，犹豫了好一会儿，后面排队的人也有点急。要不试营业这段时间，先把招牌的六七款放在菜单最显眼的位置，其他的放到背面？我是真觉得这家店能做起来，才跟你说这些。
cases.note: 试营业正是能改的时候：只挑一个问题，说成自己点单时的感受，再给一个马上能试的办法。

cases.situation: My friend Marcus wants to quit his warehouse job in the spring and put his $20,000 savings into a taco truck. He had me over to taste the menu and asked for my honest opinion. The food was genuinely great, especially the birria, but when I asked how many tacos a day he'd need to sell to cover costs, he said he hadn't worked that out yet.
cases.reply: The birria was the standout for me, and the whole menu tasted like something people would queue for. The one thing I keep coming back to is the question from the other night: how many tacos a day you'd need to sell to cover costs. Before the $20,000 goes in, could you work that number out, maybe even test it with a few weekend pop-ups while you're still at the warehouse? I'm asking because I want this to work, not because I doubt the food.
cases.note: Specific praise for the food, then the missing break-even number as a question, because it is the one thing that protects his savings.

cases.situation: 表妹小雨10月10日周六要去纹身，把设计稿发给我问真实意见：手腕内侧一只小猫，尾巴绕成一个圈，下面是奶奶的名字“秀兰”。猫画得很可爱，但名字的字又细又小，我自己脚踝上那行小字三年后就有点糊了。
cases.reply: 小雨，稿子我仔细看了，小猫太可爱了，尾巴绕成一个圈那里特别有你的感觉。我唯一有点担心的是奶奶的名字：字这么细这么小，我脚踝上那行小字三年后就有点糊了。要不要跟纹身师商量一下，把“秀兰”放大一点、笔画加粗？离10号还有时间改，我是想让它十年后看着也跟现在一样好看。
cases.note: 纹身还没做，正是能改的时候：只提一个会随时间变坏的问题，用自己的经历来说，不评价她选的图案。

cases.situation: 表姐怀孕七个月，打算给女儿起名“林梓涵”，发微信问我真实意见。我很喜欢“涵”字，她说是希望孩子有涵养。但“梓涵”这几年特别常见，我女儿班上就有两个梓涵。
cases.reply: “涵”这个字选得真好，有涵养这个寓意我特别喜欢。你让我说真话，我就提一点：“梓涵”这几年挺多的，我女儿班上就有两个，老师点名都得带姓。要不保留“涵”，前面换个少见点的字？你们定什么我都喜欢，只是觉得这个名字值得独一无二。
cases.note: 只提一个问题，并用自己亲眼见到的例子说明；最后决定权明确交还给她。

cases.situation: 我妈退休后开始在短视频平台上发自己做家常菜的视频，已经发了十几条，让我说说真实意见。我最喜欢红烧肉那条，她边做边讲特别亲切。就是每条都有5分钟左右，开头差不多两分钟在聊买菜和家长里短，真正做菜要等好久。
cases.reply: 妈，你最近几条我都看完了，红烧肉那条我看着都饿了，你边做边讲的样子特别亲切，像在家里厨房听你说话。我就提一点：开头聊买菜那两分钟，我看的时候有点着急，想快点看你下锅。要不试试一开头先放做好的菜，然后直接开始做，聊天的话放到炖的时候说？你讲得这么好，我是想让更多人一直看到最后。
cases.note: 给长辈的意见也只提一个，用“我看的时候”说感受，再给一个马上能试的做法。

cases.situation: 大学同学阿泽想从销售转行做数据分析，把简历发我让我提真实意见，下周一开始投。他自学半年做了一个分析外卖平台评论的项目，写得很扎实，但放在第二页最底下，第一页全是以前做销售的经历。
cases.reply: 阿泽，简历我认真看了。外卖评论那个项目写得特别扎实，一看就是真下了半年功夫。我唯一的担心是它在第二页最底下，我是一路翻到最后才看到的，招聘的人可能看完第一页的销售经历就放下了。要不把这个项目挪到第一页最上面，销售经历压缩成几行？底子很好，调一下顺序，周一投出去会更有竞争力。
cases.note: 只提一个问题，用“我翻到最后才看到”说自己的阅读感受，再给一个周一前就能改好的办法。

cases.situation: My friend Jess drafted an email to her landlord about the mould in her bathroom and asked if it's okay to send tonight. The facts are strong: she reported it on 3 August and 1 September and attached photos. But the last paragraph calls him a slumlord and says she'll 'make sure everyone knows what he's like'.
cases.reply: The first part is really strong: two dates and photos, it's hard to argue with. The last paragraph is where I'd pause. I think 'slumlord' and 'make sure everyone knows' give him something to react to other than the mould. What if you ended with one clear ask instead, like the date by which you want someone to come and look at it? You're in the right here, which is exactly why I'd let the facts do the work.
cases.note: She asked 'okay to send?', so lead with what works and name the one change before she hits send.

cases.situation: Mi pareja, Andrés, va a hacer paella para mis padres el sábado 10 de octubre, la primera vez que cocina para ellos. Anoche hizo una prueba y hoy me escribe por WhatsApp desde el trabajo: '¿Qué te pareció de verdad?'. El socarrat le salió perfecto, pero el arroz estaba bastante salado.
cases.reply: ¿De verdad de verdad? El socarrat te salió perfecto, crujiente justo como tiene que ser. Lo único que noté es que el arroz me quedó un poco salado; quizá con menos sal en el caldo ya lo tienes. Si quieres, el jueves hacemos otra prueba juntos. Te lo digo porque el sábado te puede quedar buenísima.
cases.note: Un solo punto, concreto y fácil de arreglar, porque todavía hay tiempo antes del sábado.

cases.situation: My friend Sam's dad died last week and the funeral is Saturday. Sam asked me to read his eulogy draft and be honest; he has five minutes. The story about his dad waking him at 5am to fish at Lake Wren is beautiful, but most of the rest is a list of his dad's jobs and dates.
cases.reply: Sam, I read it twice. The story about your dad waking you at 5am to fish at Lake Wren is beautiful; that's him, I could see it. Where I lost him a little was the run of jobs and dates, which read more like a record than like your dad. What if you kept one line on his work and gave the rest of the five minutes to more moments like the lake? Whatever you decide, it's going to mean a lot to everyone there.
cases.note: Grief makes everything land harder: one point, framed as your experience as a reader, and if he sounds raw, say it on a call rather than by text.

cases.situation: My grandma Joan, 84, asked me on the phone why hardly anyone in the family replies to her emails. They're full of lovely news, like last week's one about the robins nesting in her porch light, but she writes everything in capital letters, and my younger cousins read that as shouting. I'm visiting her on Sunday and want to text her before then.
cases.reply: Gran, I love your emails; the one about the robins nesting in your porch light made my week. Since you asked, I think I know one reason the cousins go quiet: everything's in capital letters, and they read that as shouting, even though I know you're not. It's an easy fix, and I can show you on your tablet on Sunday. Your news is too good to go unanswered.
cases.note: She asked, so give the one real reason as how others read it, not a verdict on her, and make the fix something you do together.

cases.situation: 好朋友周周明天下午去一家律所面试行政岗，发来穿搭照片问我真实意见。米色西装外套很合身，但里面配的是一件印着大卡通图案的T恤。她衣柜里有件白衬衫，上次见她穿过。
cases.reply: 外套选得特别好，很合身，整个人看着很利落。我唯一会换的是里面那件卡通T恤，律所的面试官可能会先注意到图案，而不是你。换上你那件白衬衫会不会更稳？你本来就很适合这个岗位，我是想让人第一眼就看到这一点。
cases.note: 面试前一天还来得及改：只提一处，给一个她衣柜里现成的替换，不评价她的身材或品味。
